acme-iot: Hey team — we started seeing a big spike in 429s from our mobile fleet after the network blip at 02:03 UTC. Our dashboard shows RPM hitting quota windows even though active users are low. Any ideas?

jess: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a couple of request ids and an example of the client behavior? Is this HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 from the SDKs?

acme-iot: Request ids: r-17a3b2c9 r-17a3b2d0 r-17a3b2f1. App version 3.2.1 using our in-house mobile SDK (we use HTTP/2 with connection pooling). We also do a small batched upload every minute plus a keepalive ping every 15s.

mike: Quick hypothesis: if each HTTP/2 stream is being counted as a separate request in the RPM/TPM window, a single client could multiply quota usage. Do you see a pattern of multiple streams per connection in your client logs?

acme-iot: Yes — after the outage, devices reconnect and open 4-6 concurrent streams for telemetry + upload + keepalive. We assumed multiplexing would be cheap.

ingrid: We ran into an edge case last year where an upstream proxy counted streams individually for throttling. Ops-bot: checking recent infra deploys that could affect rate accounting...

ops-bot: noticed deploy rni-proxy v2.14.0 at 02:00 UTC with change set that adjusted stream accounting (ENG-1422 queued).

jess: That matches timeline. Mike, can you confirm whether the rate-limiter is treating streams as independent requests in the new proxy path? If yes, we should scope workaround guidance to customers.

mike: Confirmed — proxy started incrementing the RPM counter per incoming stream (not per request header). Patch queued (ENG-1422). Meanwhile, two mitigations: 1) customer-side: reduce concurrent streams to 1 or serialize uploads for ~1 hour; 2) platform-side: temporary quota bump for the affected API key to avoid immediate 429s while patch rolls out.

acme-iot: Can you share repro steps so our SDK team can validate a client-side fix? Prefer runnable snippet.

mike: Repro script (Python + httpx) to simulate the issue:

```python
# repro_streams.py
import asyncio
import httpx

async def open_streams(n):
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(http2=True, timeout=30.0) as client:
        tasks = []
        for i in range(n):
            tasks.append(client.get('https://api.redwood.example/v1/telemetry?test=1'))
        res = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
        print([r.status_code for r in res])

asyncio.run(open_streams(6))
```

Run that from a single host to see RPM jump in ~1 minute windows. Use `-n` loops to see sustained effect.

ingrid: For customer support: I recommend offering the temporary quota bump (we can do +2x RPM for 2 hours) and ask them to throttle to 1 concurrent stream in the SDK while we deploy the patch. Also capture sample `x-request-id`s for us to correlate with proxy logs.

jess: Agreed. acme-iot — we can apply a 2x RPM uplift for 2 hours now. Do you want us to enable it immediately?

acme-iot: Yes please — enable now. We'll also ship SDK change to serialize the 1-minute batch. ETA 45m.

mike: Action items: 1) Support: apply 2x temporary RPM (jess). 2) SRE: roll proxy fix to revert stream->count behavior (mike, ENG-1422). 3) Customer: ship SDK serialized uploads and reduce concurrent streams to 1 (acme-iot).

jess: Applied temp quota bump — I pushed override for api-key acme-123 (expires in 2h). Watching metrics. :eyes:

ops-bot: metric alert cleared for acme-123.rpm_window at 02:11 UTC (after quota bump).

acme-iot: Seeing 429 rate drop, thanks. We'll confirm after our SDK rollout. Any long-term guidance to avoid this class of issue?

mike: Long-term: 1) clients should minimize concurrent streams per API key for high-rate workloads; 2) platform will treat a single logical request (per headers) as one quota unit (patch forthcoming); 3) consider per-route throttles rather than per-connection counting for SDKs that multiplex many small requests.

jess: I'll keep this thread open until the SDK change is confirmed in ~1h and ENG-1422 is resolved. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
